section_summary: This section covers late July through August 1940, focusing on the downfall of the moderate Yonai Cabinet and the establishment of the second government of Prince Fumimaro Konoe. Detailed diplomatic reports analyze Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka's pro-Axis foreign policy, the official proclamation of the 'Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere', and Konoe's movement to construct a 'New National Structure' transcending Western party politics while remaining distinct from European single-party fascism. Accompanying State Department memoranda and journalistic appraisals from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, political adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck, and correspondent A. T. Steele evaluate Japan's continued economic dependence on the United States and the British Empire, emphasizing the deterrent capability of the U.S. Pacific Fleet stationed at Hawaii.

subfiles.about: Reports the foreign policy tenets formulated by incoming Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka and the revival of cabinet liaison conferences.
subfiles.summary: Section Two: Foreign Office sees Britain and France declining; Matsuoka will strengthen Axis ties, seek East Asian independence and settle China and US relations. Grew warns confrontation could lead to war.
subfiles.title: Telegram 603 (Section Two) from Tokyo regarding Japanese Foreign Policy under Matsuoka

subfiles.about: Reports press accounts of Yoshisuke Ayukawa's sudden arrival in Tokyo from Hsinking to present crucial economic and foreign policy recommendations to the Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew summarizes a Yomiuri article: Manchurian Industrial Corporation head Ayukawa flew to Tokyo to present economic and international policy recommendations to the new Konoe Cabinet, coordinated with Matsuoka and Tojo.
subfiles.title: Telegram 599 from Tokyo regarding Yoshisuke Ayukawa's Recommendations to the New Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Reports the arrival in Manila of Japanese Diet members and the travel of Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura aboard the Saipan Maru bound for Davao and the South Seas.
subfiles.summary: High Commissioner Sayre reports Japanese Diet members visited Manila and are heading to Davao; Admiral Nomura travels on the same ship, prompting police protection requests.
subfiles.title: Telegram 471 from Manila regarding Japanese Diet Members and Admiral Nomura Visiting the Philippines

subfiles.about: Reports Premier-designate Konoe's consultations with the Emperor and military leaders, and the initial selection of core cabinet ministers.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoe's audience with the Emperor and plans for a four-minister conference on non-involvement and the Axis. Chosen ministers include Tojo (War), Yoshida (Navy) and Matsuoka (Foreign).
subfiles.title: Telegram 595 from Tokyo regarding Formation of the Second Konoe Cabinet and Ministerial Selections

subfiles.about: Reports Yoshisuke Ayukawa's extended conference with Prince Konoe regarding foreign loans and economic expansion for the Manchuria Industrial Development Company.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Ayukawa met Konoe for ninety minutes on economic recommendations, including foreign loans for Manchuria Industrial Development; he urged seizing opportunities, noting the US is not the only credit source.
subfiles.title: Telegram 605 from Tokyo regarding Ayukawa's Conference with Prince Konoe on Foreign Loans

subfiles.about: Transmits the official roster of ministers selected for the newly formed second cabinet of Prince Fumimaro Konoe.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoe's cabinet slate, with Matsuoka (Foreign), Yasui (Home), Kawata (Finance), Tojo (War), Yoshida (Marine) and Hoshino as Minister Without Portfolio.
subfiles.title: Telegram 608 from Tokyo Announcing the Slate of the Second Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Reports Wilfrid Fleisher's confidential background interview with incoming Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka regarding totalitarianism and foreign relations.
subfiles.summary: Grew summarizes Matsuoka's off-record Fleisher interview: democracy is bankrupt, totalitarianism will prevail, loans cannot bridge differing systems. Fleisher found him more pro-Axis than any official he had met.
subfiles.title: Telegram 606 from Tokyo regarding Wilfrid Fleisher's Interview with Yosuke Matsuoka

subfiles.about: Provides a confidential State Department departmental summary of Tokyo telegram 606 regarding Fleisher's conversation with Matsuoka.
subfiles.summary: State Department summary of Grew's report on Fleisher's Matsuoka interview: democracy doomed, totalitarianism lasting, US economic aid talk a fallacy; his practical policy toward the US undetermined.
subfiles.title: State Department Summary of Telegram 606 regarding Fleisher's Interview with Matsuoka

subfiles.about: Confirms the formal investiture of the second Konoe Cabinet and Matsuoka's concurrent portfolio as Minister for Overseas Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Grew confirms the Konoe cabinet was invested July 22, 1940, per telegram 608; Matsuoka is also Minister for Overseas Affairs.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Tokyo Reporting the Formal Investiture of the Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Reports Premier Konoe's first press interview and his initial nationwide radio address denouncing liberal party politics.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoe's first press conference was deliberately vague. His radio address condemned parties and liberal ideas as incompatible with the national polity and urged ending economic dependence on foreign powers.
subfiles.title: Telegram 614 from Tokyo on Premier Konoe's First Press Interview and Radio Address

subfiles.about: Argues that maintaining the U.S. Battle Fleet in the Pacific and at Hawaii is essential to back potential trade embargoes and deter Japanese aggression.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Welles the threat of US embargoes restrains Japan only while the Battle Fleet stays at Hawaii; a move to the Atlantic would end the fear.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Under Secretary Sumner Welles regarding U.S. Embargoes and Fleet Deterrence

subfiles.about: Provides a detailed political analysis of the collapse of the Yonai Cabinet, Konoe's return to power, and the factors governing Japanese foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew analyzes the transition from the Yonai administration to the second Konoe Cabinet, attributing the shift to popular frustration over the protracted China war and a desire to capitalize on European Axis victories. He evaluates the new cabinet as predominantly conservative, with nationalist planners like Naoki Hoshino and Akira Kazami pushing for an economic bloc and electoral reform. Grew assesses that Japan is unlikely to make an abrupt break toward the Axis in the immediate future because of its heavy economic dependence on the United States and the British Empire for vital raw materials and export markets.
subfiles.title: Telegram 613 from Tokyo Assessing the Fall of the Yonai Cabinet and Outlook under Konoe

subfiles.about: Synthesizes Ambassador Grew's political appraisal in telegram 613 regarding the Yonai Cabinet's fall and Konoe's diplomatic constraints.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern summary of telegram 613: economic dependence blocks full Axis commitment, Yonai doubted Germany and Italy, domestic pressure unseated him, and the public hopes Konoe will end the China conflict.
subfiles.title: State Department Far Eastern Division Summary of Telegram 613

subfiles.about: Reports the resignation of Masayuki Tani as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Masayuki Tani resigned as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs after Konoe's cabinet formation.
subfiles.title: Telegram 617 from Tokyo Reporting the Resignation of Vice Foreign Minister Masayuki Tani

subfiles.about: Transmits Vice Consul Beppo R. Johansen's report of an overheard train conversation between two Japanese expressing severe distress over Japanese ventures in Manchuria and China.
subfiles.summary: Consul Merrell forwards a memorandum by Vice Consul Johansen detailing a candid conversation overheard on a passenger train between Peiping and Mukden between an educated scholar and a technical expert. The Japanese travelers expressed impassioned concern over their nation's future, asserting that developmental efforts in Manchukuo are crippled by incompetent personnel and premature economic policies. They questioned the utility of anti-British agitation, criticized state propaganda and the Diet uproar over Takao Saito, and warned that antagonizing Great Britain and the United States would lead Japan to ruin.
subfiles.title: Despatch 262 from Harbin Transmitting Vice Consul Johansen's Report of an Overheard Japanese Conversation

subfiles.about: Summarizes the official Japanese Government announcement setting forth fundamental national policies and the creation of a national defense state.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits the Foreign Office summary of the Konoe Government's fundamental policy: a defense state, a new order in Greater East Asia under Japan, Manchukuo and China, administrative reform and a simplified standard of living.
subfiles.title: Telegram 640 from Tokyo on the Japanese Government's Fundamental National Policy Outline

subfiles.about: Transmits Foreign Minister Matsuoka's public declaration on proclaiming the Imperial Way ('kodo') and creating a Greater East Asian chain of common prosperity.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards Matsuoka's statement that Japan's mission is to proclaim the Imperial Way, so all nations find their place, building East Asian common prosperity with Manchukuo and China.
subfiles.title: Telegram 642 from Tokyo Transmitting Statement by Foreign Minister Matsuoka on the 'Kodo' and Greater East Asia

subfiles.about: Reports the appointment of Chuichi Ohashi as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs succeeding Masayuki Tani.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Chuichi Ohashi, formerly Counselor to the Manchukuo Government, named Vice Foreign Minister succeeding Tani.
subfiles.title: Telegram 651 from Tokyo Reporting Chuichi Ohashi's Appointment as Vice Foreign Minister

subfiles.about: Surveys critical Tokyo press editorials regarding the vague and abstract nature of the Government's and Foreign Minister's policy pronouncements.
subfiles.summary: Grew summarizes press reactions to government policy statements: Hochi called them an abstract wishlist, Nichi Nichi found the 'new order' explanation weak, Yomiuri saw a hard line replacing Arita's approach.
subfiles.title: Telegram 654 from Tokyo on Japanese Press Reactions to Government and Foreign Policy Statements

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo telegram 657 of August 3, 1940, filed under decimal classification 756D.94/57.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram 657 (August 3, 1940) filed under 756D.94/57.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram 657 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports Foreign Minister Matsuoka's press interview given on a train en route to Shinto shrines regarding Greater East Asia and ongoing diplomacy.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Matsuoka's train interview: internal reorganization and 'positive diplomacy' for Greater East Asia prosperity; optimism about Abe-Wang Ching-wei talks, while Japan observes the other powers.
subfiles.title: Telegram 685 from Tokyo on Foreign Minister Matsuoka's Train Interview En Route to National Shrines

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo telegram 687 of August 12, 1940, filed under decimal classification 756D.94/58.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram 687 (August 12, 1940) filed under 756D.94/58.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram 687 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo telegram 693 of August 12, 1940, filed under decimal classification 756D.94/59.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Tokyo telegram 693 (August 12, 1940) filed under 756D.94/59.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram 693 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports confidential discussions with Foreign Minister Matsuoka at a dinner honoring Ambassador Steinhardt regarding domestic political reorganization and anti-foreign agitation.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Matsuoka privately said Konoe's new national structure aims to end party politics, not form one party; he disliked anti-foreign campaigns and reprimanded nationalist societies. Grew thinks he might help dampen anti-American propaganda.
subfiles.title: Telegram 740 from Tokyo on Grew's Dinner Conversation with Foreign Minister Matsuoka

subfiles.about: Transmits excerpts of Premier Konoe's address to the opening session of the Preparatory Committee for the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits excerpts of Konoe's address launching the New National Structure committee: a national defense state, rejecting Western single-party dictatorship as incompatible with 'one sovereign over all'.
subfiles.title: Telegram 759 from Tokyo Transmitting Excerpts of Premier Konoe's Address on the New National Structure

subfiles.about: Reports the appointments of Toshio Shiratori and Ryoei Saito as Diplomatic Advisers to the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Toshio Shiratori and Ryoei Saito appointed Diplomatic Advisers to the Foreign Office, with Saito's career outlined.
subfiles.title: Telegram 758 from Tokyo Reporting the Appointments of Toshio Shiratori and Ryoei Saito as Diplomatic Advisers

subfiles.about: Transmits the complete text in seven sections of Premier Konoe's opening address on the establishment of the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits the full seven-section official translation of Premier Konoe's address opening the Preparatory Committee for the New National Structure on August 28, 1940. Konoe detailed the permanent necessity of mobilizing total national energies across politics, economics, and culture to conclude the China Affair and create a new order in East Asia. He explained that while parliamentary party politics founded on liberalism are obsolete, a totalitarian single-party system where one party monopolizes the state is unacceptable under Japanese polity, which requires all subjects unitedly to obey Imperial decisions and assist the Throne.
subfiles.title: Telegram 760 from Tokyo Transmitting Full Text of Premier Konoe's Address on the New National Structure

subfiles.about: Transmits an analytical six-section report by Chicago Daily News correspondent A. T. Steele regarding political trends in Japan, German-Japanese relations, and American policy.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Robert L. Smyth transmits a detailed six-section report prepared by seasoned foreign correspondent A. T. Steele following his observations in Japan and Manchuria. Steele reports that Japan is rapidly embracing totalitarianism and pro-Axis opportunism in hopes of exploiting an early German victory over Britain, though Tokyo remains cautious due to Soviet Manchurian border vulnerabilities and China commitments. Steele notes that Germans view Japan opportunistically as a nuisance factor against the United States, and he strongly advises Washington that firmness and naval strength represent the safest American policy, as Japan is anxious to avoid a conflict with the United States unless forced as a last resort.
subfiles.title: Telegram 300 from Peiping Transmitting A. T. Steele's Observations on Japan, Axis Alignment, and U.S. Policy
